sources.entry: QuikFlow - Create flowcharts with a mind-mapping workflow.

summary.name: QuikFlow
summary.one_liner: QuikFlow is a flowchart and mind-mapping app where the layout arranges itself automatically as you build the diagram.
use_cases: Drawing flowcharts that loop back or converge without manual layout
Brainstorming with a mind-map style workflow that turns into a flow
Exporting diagrams as PDF or PNG for sharing
Exporting flows to OPML, Markdown, Mermaid or JSON
summary.what_it_does: The page describes QuikFlow as a tool for creating flowcharts and mind maps using the same intuitive workflow, without the restrictions of a pure mind map. Users define elements and their relationships, and the layout updates automatically while editing; drag-and-drop can be used to reposition elements. Flows can converge or loop back, and subflows can be pasted into the middle of a flow. Sharing is through PDF and PNG export, and the comparison table also lists export to OPML, Markdown, Mermaid and JSON for Pro users.
notable: Automatic layout that adapts as the flow changes
Flows can converge or loop back, unlike typical mind maps
Free editor remains usable for viewing and editing files after cancelling Pro
caveats: Pro features require a subscription ($1.99/month or $12.99/year) or a one-time $29.99 lifetime purchase, prices vary by region
Several features such as PDF/PNG export, horizontal layouts, unlimited nodes and interactive tasks are listed as Pro-only in the comparison table
Platform names are inferred from the store links; the page itself names the Microsoft Store and Apple App Store only
